newsitem.title: CHINA: Acer announces price cut in China.
newsitem.headline: Acer announces price cut in China.

text.p: Acer, one of Taiwan's major computer manufacturers, has cut the price of its products by 20 percent with the start of production in China, where overheads are cheaper, the Business News said on Thursday.

The price cuts applied to Acer's personal computers (PCs), and notebook and service computers, the newspaper said, adding that production in China would lower costs, increase supply and shorten transportation time.
Competition from other foreign manufacturers kept Acer's China market share to only four percent in 1996, industry analysts said.
The analysts have said foreign companies' share of China's PC market fell by up to 30 percent in the past year, mainly because of a strong challenge from cheaper domestic name-brand computers.
The average price of domestic brand computers was about 10,000 yuan ($1,205), at least $300 cheaper than equivalent foreign models, they said.
China's domestic name-brand PCs increased their domestic market share to 27 percent in 1996 from 15 percent the year before, they said.
